note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Mukherjee & Maiti 2008 (Records of the Zoological Survey of India 108(1): 1-8, Ahmaditermes sikkimensis sp. nov.); the original is in English and describes the soldier only, records the alate as Unknown, and lists workers only in the type material (Paratype Workers) without a morphological description, so no worker section is given. Table 67 also gives measurements of the compared species A. emersoni: the middle 'Known Range' column (0.90—1.00, 0.83—0.93, 0.46—0.60, 0.14—0.20, 0.37—0.53 and so on) belongs to A. emersoni, while this species has only single holotype values and no ranges; the header and column order were displaced by OCR and cross-checked against the Comparison section (original: 'head-width 1.00 mm (vs. head narrower, 0.83-0.93 mm in A. emersoni)'). sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Of the two species previously known from the Indian subcontinent, A. pyricephalus has a dimorphic soldier, whereas the soldier of this species is monomorphic. The species is closely related to A. emersoni (Maiti) from the eastern Himalayas and differs as follows: head wider, head width 1.00 mm (0.83—0.93 mm in A. emersoni); posterior margin of the head distinctly concave (nearly straight in A. emersoni); dorsal outline of the head almost straight, with only a very weak elevation at the base of the rostrum (in A. emersoni the dorsal outline of the head is incurved, without a distinct elevation). The alate is recorded as unknown in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head pale brown; rostrum yellow-brown, darker apically. Antennae, pronotum and abdominal tergites pale brown. Head and pronotum with sparse fine hairs; abdominal hairs more erect.
Head (excluding antennae) subpyriform, with a distinct constriction behind the antennal bases; head slightly longer than wide, widest posteriorly, slightly less than the width at the constriction below the antennae, lateral margins strongly convex. Posterior margin broadly rounded, with a distinct median concavity; dorsal outline of the head almost straight, with a weak elevation at the base of the rostrum only; posterior elevation of the head moderate (0.42 mm). Rostrum short, subcylindrical, slightly longer than half the head length, with several fine hairs apically. Fontanelle gland and its duct distinct. Antennae broken, segment 2 slightly thicker than segment 3, segment 3 smaller than segment 2 and twice segments 4 and 5, the following segments gradually increasing in length and width, densely pilose. Labrum small, wider than long. Anteclypeus white, much wider than long, anterior margin convex; postclypeus distinct, anterior margin convex. Mandibles reduced, small, without any teeth or spine-like processes. Margin of the molar plate irregular. Postmentum wider than long, widest medially, anterior and posterior margins nearly straight. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, anterior margin with a weak median concavity, posterior margin weakly convex.
Measurements (mm, holotype soldier): head length including rostrum 1.57; head length excluding rostrum 1.00; maximum head width 1.00; head width at the constriction 0.61; posterior elevation of the head 0.42; head index (width/length excluding rostrum) 1.00; rostrum length (base of left mandible to rostral apex) 0.57; maximum pronotal length 0.15; maximum pronotal width 0.45; pronotal index (length/width) 0.33. Antennae of the holotype broken, number of segments unknown (this column reads '—' for this species in Table 67).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Recorded as Unknown (Imago) in the original, not described.
